case_goals.tinos-demo-allow-then-interval-denial: Run only the positive case with pinned Artemis runner 9f8ef4868f9eb1d8f01526fef393db762f9f2ef6, profile pro, app com.dualix.dualmessenger.webscanner, test ad IDs only, placement main, minimum interval 20 seconds, and maximum 3 shows per hour. Use a fresh cold start without clearing app data. Complete only presented Splash/UMP consent, Language First-Open, Privacy Ack, Forced Re-Login, and Onboarding screens; never enter personal credentials or invent account state. If Home needs personal data or is unavailable, report NOT-RUN. Dismiss the automatic Premium paywall with Android system Back without purchase. Confirm Home and visible DiscountBadge (non-premium). Find visible labels "WhatsApp" and "Direct Message" in the UI tree; note the Direct Message row's UI-tree element index without tapping it during setup. Select the WhatsApp tab by its UI-tree element index with times=1, never by a coordinate pair. For both labels, accept UI-tree text only when it equals the label or its first line or first comma-separated part equals the label. If either element is missing, report NOT-RUN. Do not use Compose test tags or hidden resource identifiers. Start the reviewed exact-serial TinosDemo capture wrapper before the first case feature tap; do not start another logger or clear buffers. Identify exactly two planned tap steps in this session's steps rows whose action is tap and target_text equals Direct Message or has that label as its first line or first comma-separated part. For each matching feature tap, require exactly one successful same-session action trace linked by step_id with type=action, name=tap, status=success, payload success=true, and matching target_text, target_bounds, target_resource_id, and target_class; ignore coordinates and normalized_coordinates because runner self-healing can change them. Reject any matched feature action or trace whose times is present and not integer 1. The steps timestamp is the planned turn, not tap evidence. The trace timestamp and duration bound the dispatch interval, extended by a later payload end timestamp. Missing, ambiguous, failed, or malformed traces are INVALID-EVIDENCE. The verifier reports the planned timestamp, unmodified target_text, trace ID, and dispatch interval; use the interval upper bound for timing and event ordering. Require all recognized Tinos logs strictly after the first tap dispatch interval upper bound and inside the native session step window; require any second-tap outcome log after its dispatch interval upper bound. Positive mode requires exactly two matching taps; control requires exactly one. Include each tap observation in the report; never enter tap timestamps manually. Read first-visible and close-control timestamps from the recording, normalized to host epoch; these are the only action-time verifier inputs. After capture starts, tap the "Direct Message" feature row once with times=1 by its UI-tree element index; never use a coordinate pair. Close the displayed ad with its visible close control within 15 seconds of first visibility, or report NOT-RUN. Require `show allowed: shown and dismissed`; if absent after a close within 15 seconds, report NOT-RUN for the show-call timeout race. Require `revenue <valueMicros> micros <currency> unit=ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/1033173712 network=<network> precision=<precision>` or FAIL: revenue_event_missing. Return Home exactly once with Android system Back, then confirm visible labels "WhatsApp" and "Direct Message" using the same matching rule. Let D be first-ad visible duration, t1 the first exact allow-log timestamp after dismissal, and t2 the upper bound of the second tap's successful action-trace dispatch interval. Tap a second time only if `t2 - t1 <= 15 seconds - D` and `(t2 - t1) + D + 5 seconds <= 20 seconds`; 5 seconds covers up to 4 seconds for second fill and 1 second timestamp uncertainty. If `15 seconds - D <= 0`, clocks cannot align within ±1 second, Home does not return, or the timing window is missed, report NOT-RUN and do not tap late. After the timing gate, tap the same feature row once with times=1 by its UI-tree element index; never use a coordinate pair. Require `show denied by Tinos rules (NOT_ALLOWED)` after the second dispatch interval. If two allow lines and no denial occur inside the verified window, report FAIL: gate_allowed_inside_interval; outside the window report NOT-RUN. Fill failures `not loaded; skipping` and `show failed (<code>)` are neither allow nor denial and report NOT-RUN. Preserve same-session Checker and runner-bound final-capture identity. If capture or Artemis is SIGKILLed, confirm the recorded logger PID is gone before device release. Do not execute the negative control.

runtime_values_only: attempt-root: a new empty evidence directory for this case
case-goal: the complete matching case_goals string above, submitted verbatim as one argv element; do not replace it with a journey filename
case-id: the exact matching case id above
Sol-granted-exact-serial: the exact serial in Sol's issue-visible grant
fresh-UUID: a new UUID per case, reused as both session and run ID
observed-artemis-exit-status: the exact foreground Artemis process exit status

The verifier matches target_text equal to Direct Message or with that label as its first line or first comma-separated part, identifies each tap in the same session steps rows, and requires one successful same-session action trace linked by step_id with type=action, name=tap, status=success, payload success=true, and matching target text and selector. The steps timestamp is planned-turn time, not tap evidence. The trace timestamp and duration bound the dispatch interval, extended by a later payload end timestamp. Missing, ambiguous, failed, or malformed traces are INVALID-EVIDENCE. Positive requires exactly two matching taps; control requires exactly one. Report planned timestamp, unmodified target_text, trace ID, and dispatch interval in tap_observations; use the interval upper bound for timing and event ordering. Require recognized Tinos logs strictly after the first tap dispatch interval upper bound and inside the native session step window.
first-visible-epoch: recording time normalized to the native host-epoch timeline; positive-only input
closed-epoch: close-control time normalized to the native host-epoch timeline; positive-only input
log-event-epoch: device epoch timestamp mapped to host epoch with capture metadata and uncertainty
entry_point.collection: Run in the foreground; preserve the complete wrapper, runner, and verifier argv and environment, stdout/stderr, logger PID and stop status, cursor, runner and verifier exit statuses, trace directory, timestamped raw TinosDemo logcat, and same-session Checker ledger and runner-bound final capture. Control requires exactly one matching session feature tap; exit 1 with JSON fail_assertion is valid only for the intended false assertion; control exit 2 with NOT-RUN means the allow line is missing after the timeout race; other control exit 2 outcomes are invalid_control. Positive mode requires exactly two matching session feature taps. Exit 0 is PASS, exit 10 is FAIL, exit 11 is NOT-RUN, and exit 12 is INVALID-EVIDENCE. Two allow lines and no denial inside the verified timing window return exit 10 FAIL with gate_allowed_inside_interval and a separate revenue_observation field; outside the window returns exit 11 NOT-RUN before event-count classification. Both modes require Artemis exit status 0 and session-bounded timestamped evidence. If the foreground command is SIGKILLed, the wrapper trap may not stop the exact logger PID; confirm that PID is gone before device release. Do not run if execution would incur new spend.

testcase_side_tool.purpose: Validate timestamped Tinos events and same-session Checker/final-capture identity for positive and negative-control modes.

testcase_side_log_capture.purpose: Start exact-serial TinosDemo logcat with a device-epoch start cursor before Artemis, record host clock samples around the device clock probe, refuse to launch Artemis if logcat does not remain running during startup, and stop the recorded logger PID on every exit path.
